plan: In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), there's no incentive to shade my bid. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks winning at a loss. With my value at $24, the optimal bid is exactly $24 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: if you win, you pay the second-highest bid regardless of your own bid, so bidding above your value risks losses, and bidding below your value risks losing profitable auctions unnecessarily. With no repeated interaction to exploit and independent value draws, the optimal strategy is straightforward truthful bidding. I will bid exactly my value of $16 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks negative profit if you win at a price above value, while underbidding only risks losing profitable opportunities. With value $24, bidding exactly $24 maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies.
